name: DeskVNC FAQ
description: Machine readable answers to the most common questions about DeskVNC, the native VNC, RDP and SSH client with an MCP server for AI agent control of remote desktops.

mainEntity.name: Does an AI agent need to be installed on the remote machine to use DeskVNC?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. DeskVNC's MCP server drives the remote machine over the existing VNC, RDP or SSH protocol that the machine already speaks. Nothing is installed on the remote side, which is why the approach works on Citrix, on VDI, on jump hosts, and on any machine a client owns where installing an agent would be refused.

mainEntity.name: Which AI clients work with the DeskVNC MCP server?

acceptedAnswer.text: Claude Code and OpenCode are verified over both stdio and HTTP transport. Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, VS Code, and plain Python agents are documented in the project's AI agent integration notes. The AI Agents panel inside the DeskVNC app contains a one click registration button for Claude Code, and dvv doctor prints the exact registration line for any other client.

Yes. DeskVNC is free and open source, dual licensed under MIT or Apache 2.0 at the user's option. There is no account, no telemetry, and no paid tier holding a feature back. Sponsoring the project on GitHub Sponsors funds the roadmap and the signed Windows builds.

mainEntity.name: Which remote desktop protocols does DeskVNC support?

acceptedAnswer.text: DeskVNC speaks VNC, RDP and SSH. The VNC core covers RFB 3.3 through 3.8 with every common encoding, VeNCrypt, RA2 and Apple authentication, and continuous updates, tested against x11vnc, TigerVNC, QEMU, RealVNC, and macOS Screen Sharing. The RDP core covers Windows desktops with NLA, RemoteApp, resolution control, and the usual codecs. The SSH core gives a terminal that survives a drop, SFTP transfers, tunnels, and PuTTY key files.

mainEntity.name: Which platforms does DeskVNC run on?

acceptedAnswer.text: DeskVNC runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. The macOS build is signed and notarized and opens normally. The Windows installer is signed. The Linux build ships as an x86_64 binary in a tarball. Building from source requires Rust 1.95 or newer, Node 22 or newer, and the Tauri 2 system dependencies for the host platform.

mainEntity.name: How fast is the DeskVNC MCP server?

acceptedAnswer.text: Measured against a real 1920x1080 Windows desktop on a LAN: dvv_open and attach in 4 ms, dvv_control acquire in under 1 ms, dvv_screen at scale 0.25 in 25 ms, dvv_screen at full scale in 70 ms, and one observe then act cycle in 19 ms, which is about 52 actions per second. dvv_type reaches 447 characters per second at wpm 12000.

mainEntity.name: Can a human take control back while an AI agent is driving a session?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A person can click into the pane at any moment and the agent is fenced out of that session. Held keys and pressed buttons are released so a half finished drag cannot strand the desktop. The agent resumes when the pane is released back to it.

mainEntity.name: Can a single agent control many machines at once?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Every machine is its own limb with its own lease, so ten machines are ten independent loops that one agent can drive in parallel. The local mouse and keyboard are never involved: input goes over the protocol, the window can be minimised, and the operator carries on using their own computer.

Credentials live in the operating system keychain: Keychain Services on macOS, Credential Manager on Windows, and Secret Service on Linux. An encrypted file fallback is available for headless machines. A test in the project asserts that saving a host writes nothing sensitive into the profile database.

mainEntity.name: What is the dvv MCP server?

acceptedAnswer.text: dvv is the Model Context Protocol server that ships with DeskVNC. It hands an AI agent the same VNC, RDP and SSH connections a person uses. The agent opens one of the saved machines, observes the screen, and sends clicks and keystrokes over the existing protocol. Tools include dvv_hosts, dvv_open, dvv_control, dvv_screen, dvv_click, dvv_type, dvv_key, dvv_files, dvv_clipboard, dvv_term_read, dvv_term_send, dvv_run, dvv_wait, and the dvv_group family.

mainEntity.name: Does the DeskVNC MCP server install anything on the remote machine?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The MCP server runs on the operator's machine. Remote input is sent over the existing VNC, RDP or SSH protocol, so no software is installed on the target. This is the property that lets the agent reach Citrix, VDI, jump hosts, and other locked down desktops where installing an agent would be refused.

mainEntity.name: How does the agent loop work?

acceptedAnswer.text: The loop is four steps. dvv_hosts lists the saved machines. dvv_open opens one and returns a limb id, the screen size, and the state. dvv_control acquires the wheel on the limb. Then the agent alternates dvv_screen to look and dvv_click, dvv_type, or dvv_key to act, passing the screen generation returned by dvv_screen on each click so a click computed against a stale screen is refused.

mainEntity.name: What stops an agent from clicking on a stale screen?

acceptedAnswer.text: Coordinate fencing. Every dvv_screen response carries a generation. dvv_click requires the agent to pass that generation, and a click computed against a stale screen is refused. dvv_type and dvv_key are also refused with SCREEN_CHANGED if something large has repainted since the agent last looked, because focus moves when a window opens. There is no override.

mainEntity.name: Does DeskVNC support attended support sessions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A separate DeskVNC Support build ships on the same release page. The recipient presses Get a code or Create invitation, approves the connection, and the operator connects through Boundary support inside DeskVNC. Boundary tries a direct encrypted path first and uses its relay fallback when the networks do not allow a direct path. No account is required for an attended support session.

mainEntity.name: What license is DeskVNC released under?

acceptedAnswer.text: DeskVNC is dual licensed under either the MIT License or the Apache License, Version 2.0, at the user's option. The full texts are in LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE in the repository, and contributions are accepted under the same dual license unless the contributor states otherwise.

mainEntity.name: Where can I get the latest DeskVNC release?

acceptedAnswer.text: The latest release, with signed installers for Windows, signed and notarized builds for macOS, and an x86_64 Linux tarball, is published at https://github.com/psmux/DeskVNC/releases/latest. The changelog at https://github.com/psmux/DeskVNC/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md records every release.

mainEntity.name: How do I report a bug or a server that DeskVNC mishandles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open an issue at https://github.com/psmux/DeskVNC/issues. For interoperability findings, name the server and its version; several releases exist because someone did exactly that. For security issues, follow the private channel in SECURITY.md rather than opening a public issue.
